resolvedQuestions.text: Which failures were latent, and what properties make a fallback-only path invisible in production?
How do you detect a latent fallback defect before promoting the fallback to primary?
What residue classes does a transport removal leave behind, and which file carries each?
Which residue classes does tooling find unaided, and which only reading finds?
What repeatable checklist for the next migration fails cheaply at every step, and where is the packet record wrong?

keyFindings.statement: A fallback-only path fails latently via order-gated execution, unverified preconditions, and masked failure; masking is operative because the degradation is already correctly explained by the primary's failure.
The flat socket path was two owners computing one derived path, not a typo; the default socket directory is the one the bridge always scopes.
Promotion converts a defect of exposure zero into exposure one; the audit belongs to the promotion commit and is scoped by what the promoted path reads.
An env alias chain was renamed into a duplicate of itself at six sites, leaving the second spelling unreachable while a test still deletes it; pre-existing, and a live specimen of residue class R8.
Three harnesses each scoped to a component, none to the composition where the fallback lives, so their combined green was not evidence about the seam.
Seven promotion-time checks ordered by cost; only invocation inversion with a byte diff has a proven catch, and it is the only one requiring a captured before-image.
A pre-flight probe that duplicates a derivation cannot detect its own duplication; it amplifies a premise error into a fast, well-labelled refusal.
In a failure-only path, a comment that justifies the path's premise marks the line where an unverified assumption is load-bearing.
Eight residue classes, each with a carrier, a dead referent and a different instrument.
The deleted config blocks carried documentation keys alongside values; the values were re-homed to the launcher, the documentation survives only in git.
Tests encoding a removed contract are red or unresolvable, so detection is a sampling property; the rule to raise rather than rewrite preserved the count.
A name is residue only when its referent is dead; identical tokens (mcpServerDir vs the mcp trigger aliases) require opposite dispositions.
Generated artifacts are stale by construction, non-separably regenerable, and may carry drift their consumers depend on; they can also fence what may be renamed.
603 mcp-server/ references survive outside the swept tranche; a tranche-scoped grep returns clean while the path still resolves from outside.
The sharpest documentation residue is a live diagnostic describing the removed transport in the present tense, inviting an operator to re-register it.
Harness residue in machine state — a rewritten launcher status file, a shared generation counter, a stray daemon — is reachable by neither grep nor git.
The tooling-versus-reading split is a property of the search key: token-keyed searches miss residue that does not name the removed thing, even inside the swept directory.
R8: two live documents inside the swept tranche assert an alias the code no longer honors, because a rename rewrote both operands of the pair.
The same repository already carries the remedy: an enumerated, documented LEGACY_ALIASES table per concern, versus an inline NAME ?? NAME chain per consumer.
Classes discoverable before the removal are gates on it; classes discoverable only after are steps in a post-removal battery.
The retrieval fixture was handed from phase 5 to a phase whose scope excluded it; the handoff has no acceptance record and the item survives.
The parent's progress rows mark phases 004-008 Pending with an empty DONE WHEN table while their commits and artifacts exist; a resuming session reaches the inverse of the truth.
The packet's final limitations describe a state two commits old: the suites they report as raised-not-fixed were rewritten or retired by 9015d00c79.
A pending row can record a question that stopped being a question: F18 is headed OPEN while its resolution is in source and its phase is closed.
The fix that closed the reopened wire migration landed in a commit whose message names no phase, so no phase log owns it.
A 22-step checklist in five stages, ordered by availability tier then cost, with the availability-then-cost rule stated as its ordering principle.
The record's defects are staleness at the edges, not inflation: discarded invalid benchmarks, a self-declared premature closure, and a fast-fail fix reported as worse than the bug.

ruledOutDirections.approach: Explaining the flat socket probe as a mistyped or stale literal
ruledOutDirections.reason: The literal is the correct unscoped form of the always-scoped default directory

ruledOutDirections.approach: Treating a distinguishable fallback reason code as sufficient observability
ruledOutDirections.reason: socket_absent is in RETRYABLE_REASONS, so the caller expects it

ruledOutDirections.approach: Widening the parity harness to cover the seam
ruledOutDirections.reason: Its allowlist encodes genuine surface differences; a cross-seam equality assertion is smaller

ruledOutDirections.approach: Asserting the helper's socket path as a literal
ruledOutDirections.reason: The defective revision's own output is what such a test asserts

ruledOutDirections.approach: Treating name residue as one token-keyed class
ruledOutDirections.reason: mcpServerDir and the mcp aliases share a token and need opposite dispositions

ruledOutDirections.approach: A blanket regenerate-after-rename step for generated artifacts
ruledOutDirections.reason: One generator run rewrote 18,966 unrelated lines and shifted advisor fusion scores

ruledOutDirections.approach: Treating the env-in-block residue as a post-deletion search
ruledOutDirections.reason: The block's contents are not in the tree; the instrument is git history

ruledOutDirections.approach: Treating the seven-class taxonomy as closed
ruledOutDirections.reason: R8 appeared only when the search-key question was asked

ruledOutDirections.approach: Reading the parent's pending progress rows as a delivery failure
ruledOutDirections.reason: Every phase's artifacts exist; the rows are a reconciliation failure

ruledOutDirections.approach: Reproducing the brief's 26 tests / 7 registration assertions
ruledOutDirections.reason: The suites count 9+1, 4 and 22 frozen cases with 27-of-41 failing; the figure is in no packet artifact

residueClasses.name: config env whose holder died
residueClasses.foundBy: reading the deletion diff (git history, not the tree)

residueClasses.name: tests encoding the removed contract
residueClasses.foundBy: tooling, when a full suite is sampled

residueClasses.name: names outliving referents
residueClasses.foundBy: human judgement; the token is visible, the referent is not

residueClasses.name: generated artifacts
residueClasses.foundBy: tooling finds the strings; the generator's contract explains the deferral

residueClasses.name: cross-package hardcoded paths
residueClasses.foundBy: path-shaped grep, run outside the swept tranche

residueClasses.name: documentation describing a deleted harness
residueClasses.foundBy: grep finds strings; reading finds tense and consequence

residueClasses.name: local machine state outside the repository
residueClasses.foundBy: neither grep nor suite; a run's side effects

residueClasses.name: alias pairs collapsed by a rename
residueClasses.foundBy: a concept-keyed grep (legacy/alias/fallback), not a token grep
